summary: Coin has no designer guide for Title; use its facts from the package types.

examples.purpose: A screen title with a subtitle.
examples.jsx: <Title title="Accounts" subtitle="Linked to JioFinance" modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }} />

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Optional subtitle displayed below the title.

props.name: textAlign
props.description: Horizontal alignment of the title text. Default "Left", from the component source.

props.name: subtitleStyle
props.description: Optional style overrides for the subtitle text.

props.name: disableTruncation
props.description: When `true`, disables truncation for both the title and subtitle: the trailing ellipsis (`…`) is never shown and the `numberOfLines` clamp is ignored. The text is also never shrunk by a tight parent — it keeps its full intrinsic size and overflows (even breaking the parent layout) rather than ever clipping into an ellipsis. The text still wraps onto multiple lines.

props.name: singleLine
props.description: When `true`, forces both the title and subtitle onto a single line with no wrapping (implies {@link disableTruncation}). On web the line overflows horizontally — brutally breaking the parent layout if it has to — instead of wrapping or truncating.

props.name: ...React.ComponentProps<typeof View>
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.

modes.name: Color Mode
modes.description: A token collection Title reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.
